The first and third compile the by-value form\0A// (the buffer element is passed as a function argument); the second and fourth compile\0A// the direct-indexing form. Everything else is identical.\0A//\0A// What to compare: in each pane, where the float-typed structured-buffer load sits\0A// relative to the first conditional branch. In the by-value panes both loads are in the\0A// entry block above a single branch, and the two [branch] conditions have been folded\0A// into one. In the direct-indexing panes the integer load comes first, then a branch,\0A// and the float load is inside the guarded block, so it runs only when the first\0A// condition holds. !48 = !{!"/app/example.hlsl", !"//==========================================================================//\0A// Four panes, one source, two compilers. The first and third compile the by-value form\0A// (the buffer element is passed as a function argument); the second and fourth compile\0A// the direct-indexing form. Everything else is identical.\0A//\0A// What to compare: in each pane, where the float-typed structured-buffer load sits\0A// relative to the first conditional branch. In the by-value panes both loads are in the\0A// entry block above a single branch, and the two [branch] conditions have been folded\0A// into one. In the direct-indexing panes the integer load comes first, then a branch,\0A// and the float load is inside the guarded block, so it runs only when the first\0A// condition holds. That one load is the reported cost. Both forms are correct code; the\0A// difference is where the memory access ends up. The last two panes are the in-progress\0A// Clang HLSL compiler on the same input.\0A//\0A// This source is a restating of the shader in the issue body: the pixel stage becomes\0A// [numthreads] and discard becomes a store to an RWBuffer, because clang-dxc rejects\0A// discard today and a pane full of that error would say nothing about this issue. The\0A// original pixel spelling was measured locally instead, on a Debug build of main and on\0A// 20 stable releases back to v1.4.1907, and this restating was checked to still show\0A// the same difference before it was published here.\0A//\0A// Compiler Explorer builds these with debug flags appended, which changes value names\0A// and adds metadata but not the placement being compared.\0A//==========================================================================//\0A\0A// Compute-shader restating of repro.hlsl, agent-constructed.\0A//\0A// Why: Compiler Explorer's clang-dxc panes cannot compile the original -- clang\0A// answers `error: use of undeclared identifier 'discard'`, so a Clang pane on\0A// repro.hlsl is noise about an unimplemented intrinsic and says nothing about this\0A// issue.  This file replaces `discard` with a store to an RWBuffer and the pixel\0A// stage with [numthreads], keeping everything the issue is about: the by-value\0A// struct parameter in test1, the direct indexing in test2, both [branch] hints, and\0A// the same field layout.\0A//\0A// SKILL step 7 requires a transformed repro to be re-checked before it is trusted.\0A// The check is local and captured:\0A//     variant-cs-test1-main-debug.txt   -T cs_6_0 -E test1  --expect match\0A//     variant-cs-test2-main-debug.txt   -T cs_6_0 -E test2  --expect no-match\0A// i.e. the asymmetry must survive the translation, scored by the same match.json.\0A\0Astruct SData\0A{\0A\09float3 value;\0A\09uint type;\0A\09float4 value2;\0A};\0A\0AStructuredBuffer<SData> dataBuffer;\0ARWBuffer<float> outBuf;\0A\0Avoid fct1(SData data)\0A{\0A\09[branch]if (data.type == 0)\0A\09\09[branch] if(data.value.x < 0.0f)\0A\09\09\09outBuf[0] = 1.0f;\0A}\0A\0A[numthreads(1, 1, 1)]\0Avoid test1()\0A{\0A\09fct1(dataBuffer[0]);\0A}\0A\0Avoid fct2(int id)\0A{\0A\09[branch] if (dataBuffer[id].type == 0)\0A\09\09[branch] if (dataBuffer[id].value.x < 0.0f)\0A\09\09      outBuf[0] = 1.0f;\0A}\0A\0A[numthreads(1, 1, 1)]\0Avoid test2()\0A{\0A\09fct2(0);\0A}\0A"}

!113 = !{!"/app/example.hlsl", !"//==========================================================================//\0A// Four panes, one source, two compilers. The first and third compile the by-value form\0A// (the buffer element is passed as a function argument); the second and fourth compile\0A// the direct-indexing form. Everything else is identical.\0A//\0A// What to compare: in each pane, where the float-typed structured-buffer load sits\0A// relative to the first conditional branch. In the by-value panes both loads are in the\0A// entry block above a single branch, and the two [branch] conditions have been folded\0A// into one. In the direct-indexing panes the integer load comes first, then a branch,\0A// and the float load is inside the guarded block, so it runs only when the first\0A// condition holds. That one load is the reported cost. Both forms are correct code; the\0A// difference is where the memory access ends up. The last two panes are the in-progress\0A// Clang HLSL compiler on the same input.\0A//\0A// This source is a restating of the shader in the issue body: the pixel stage becomes\0A// [numthreads] and discard becomes a store to an RWBuffer, because clang-dxc rejects\0A// discard today and a pane full of that error would say nothing about this issue. The\0A// original pixel spelling was measured locally instead, on a Debug build of main and on\0A// 20 stable releases back to v1.4.1907, and this restating was checked to still show\0A// the same difference before it was published here.\0A//\0A// Compiler Explorer builds these with debug flags appended, which changes value names\0A// and adds metadata but not the placement being compared.\0A//==========================================================================//\0A\0A// Compute-shader restating of repro.hlsl, agent-constructed.\0A//\0A// Why: Compiler Explorer's clang-dxc panes cannot compile the original -- clang\0A// answers `error: use of undeclared identifier 'discard'`, so a Clang pane on\0A// repro.hlsl is noise about an unimplemented intrinsic and says nothing about this\0A// issue.  This file replaces `discard` with a store to an RWBuffer and the pixel\0A// stage with [numthreads], keeping everything the issue is about: the by-value\0A// struct parameter in test1, the direct indexing in test2, both [branch] hints, and\0A// the same field layout.\0A//\0A// SKILL step 7 requires a transformed repro to be re-checked before it is trusted.\0A// The check is local and captured:\0A//     variant-cs-test1-main-debug.txt   -T cs_6_0 -E test1  --expect match\0A//     variant-cs-test2-main-debug.txt   -T cs_6_0 -E test2  --expect no-match\0A// i.e. the asymmetry must survive the translation, scored by the same match.json.\0A\0Astruct SData\0A{\0A\09float3 value;\0A\09uint type;\0A\09float4 value2;\0A};\0A\0AStructuredBuffer<SData> dataBuffer;\0ARWBuffer<float> outBuf;\0A\0Avoid fct1(SData data)\0A{\0A\09[branch]if (data.type == 0)\0A\09\09[branch] if(data.value.x < 0.0f)\0A\09\09\09outBuf[0] = 1.0f;\0A}\0A\0A[numthreads(1, 1, 1)]\0Avoid test1()\0A{\0A\09fct1(dataBuffer[0]);\0A}\0A\0Avoid fct2(int id)\0A{\0A\09[branch] if (dataBuffer[id].type == 0)\0A\09\09[branch] if (dataBuffer[id].value.x < 0.0f)\0A\09\09      outBuf[0] = 1.0f;\0A}\0A\0A[numthreads(1, 1, 1)]\0Avoid test2()\0A{\0A\09fct2(0);\0A}\0A"}
!114 = !{}

!112 = !{i32 1, i32 8}
!113 = !{!"/app/example.hlsl", !"//==========================================================================//\0A// Four panes, one source, two compilers. The first and third compile the by-value form\0A// (the buffer element is passed as a function argument); the second and fourth compile\0A// the direct-indexing form. Everything else is identical.\0A//\0A// What to compare: in each pane, where the float-typed structured-buffer load sits\0A// relative to the first conditional branch. In the by-value panes both loads are in the\0A// entry block above a single branch, and the two [branch] conditions have been folded\0A// into one. In the direct-indexing panes the integer load comes first, then a branch,\0A// and the float load is inside the guarded block, so it runs only when the first\0A// condition holds. That one load is the reported cost. Both forms are correct code; the\0A// difference is where the memory access ends up. The last two panes are the in-progress\0A// Clang HLSL compiler on the same input.\0A//\0A// This source is a restating of the shader in the issue body: the pixel stage becomes\0A// [numthreads] and discard becomes a store to an RWBuffer, because clang-dxc rejects\0A// discard today and a pane full of that error would say nothing about this issue. The\0A// original pixel spelling was measured locally instead, on a Debug build of main and on\0A// 20 stable releases back to v1.4.1907, and this restating was checked to still show\0A// the same difference before it was published here.\0A//\0A// Compiler Explorer builds these with debug flags appended, which changes value names\0A// and adds metadata but not the placement being compared.\0A//==========================================================================//\0A\0A// Compute-shader restating of repro.hlsl, agent-constructed.\0A//\0A// Why: Compiler Explorer's clang-dxc panes cannot compile the original -- clang\0A// answers `error: use of undeclared identifier 'discard'`, so a Clang pane on\0A// repro.hlsl is noise about an unimplemented intrinsic and says nothing about this\0A// issue.  This file replaces `discard` with a store to an RWBuffer and the pixel\0A// stage with [numthreads], keeping everything the issue is about: the by-value\0A// struct parameter in test1, the direct indexing in test2, both [branch] hints, and\0A// the same field layout.\0A//\0A// SKILL step 7 requires a transformed repro to be re-checked before it is trusted.\0A// The check is local and captured:\0A//     variant-cs-test1-main-debug.txt   -T cs_6_0 -E test1  --expect match\0A//     variant-cs-test2-main-debug.txt   -T cs_6_0 -E test2  --expect no-match\0A// i.e. the asymmetry must survive the translation, scored by the same match.json.\0A\0Astruct SData\0A{\0A\09float3 value;\0A\09uint type;\0A\09float4 value2;\0A};\0A\0AStructuredBuffer<SData> dataBuffer;\0ARWBuffer<float> outBuf;\0A\0Avoid fct1(SData data)\0A{\0A\09[branch]if (data.type == 0)\0A\09\09[branch] if(data.value.x < 0.0f)\0A\09\09\09outBuf[0] = 1.0f;\0A}\0A\0A[numthreads(1, 1, 1)]\0Avoid test1()\0A{\0A\09fct1(dataBuffer[0]);\0A}\0A\0Avoid fct2(int id)\0A{\0A\09[branch] if (dataBuffer[id].type == 0)\0A\09\09[branch] if (dataBuffer[id].value.x < 0.0f)\0A\09\09      outBuf[0] = 1.0f;\0A}\0A\0A[numthreads(1, 1, 1)]\0Avoid test2()\0A{\0A\09fct2(0);\0A}\0A"}
